First, we asked crowd workers to evaluate semantic correctness. We gave crowd workers an utterance and asked them to assign one of the four provided intent descriptions; a correct option was among them... Second, we asked crowd workers to evaluate the fluency of generated utterances. Crowd workers were provided with an utterance and were asked to score it on a Likert-type scale from 1 to 5, where (5) means that the utterance sounds natural, (3) means that the utterance contains some errors, (1) means that it is hard or even impossible to understand the utterance.
